epistemic status: personal anecdote

should we go on a date? 

I’m more than happy to meet and go on a date should our Nash equilibrium⁠ works out. If you are interested in me as a friend, then I have a friends-equivalent doc. I love to meet new people, well… what is life if not the people you share it with?


Dating is a notorious numbers game, and us triathletes are infamous for being lethargic1 after work and brick sessions. I also don’t like to repeat myself, therefore, making a dating docs seems like an reasonable next thing—something I can share with someone I find attractive.
Most people know me online as aarnphm /urn-fm/, but you can call me Aaron (or a-a-ron). I was born in ‘01. I work on ML system and make sure they behave themselves. I’m hoping to find a wonderful woman to be my partner2, someone I can share a life with for many years to come ♥

Here’s me in 30 seconds. By all means explore the rest of the documents.3
I’m love and obssessed with what I do. Other’s wellfare and working on hard problems⁠ are things I care a lot about. But most importantly, I want to share a life with someone and build a family with. I work a lot—it’s all I do these days—but I also want to build for something more than just myself. I’m lucky to date a lot of amazing women and men, but always the wrong timing or we aren’t aligned for the same thing. Hence, this document is more/less an encapsulation of what I want as well as the life I wish for as earnestly and openly as possible.
I don’t really care what you do, as long as there are subjects/topics that excite you: beauty of math and science, the amazing feats of human engineering, the drive to help people, etc. I also value my relationship with my friends. I also travel around with my bike a lot.
I’m the 3am call who shows up, so I’m reliable4. I was poly with several partners; my last relationship, however, showed me I’m better suited to monogamy.
My love languages⁠ are physical touch and quality time. I’m “securely attached”⁠. I’m a bit of a free spirit, possibly due to the fact that I moved continents at a young age.
My Myers-Briggs is ENTJ-A, though it often swings to INTJ-T.5
I like them em-dash (—) (contrary to many, many recent beliefs), parentheticals and non-sequiturs.
I listen to quite a bit of Rachmaninoff, Bill Evans, UK garage, and often find myself rabbit-holing on random math topics.

about me.
I’m an honest person, and I’m not afraid to admit to mistakes. I’m sure I’ll make even more mistakes, but no one is ✨ perfect ✨ and we only have one life to live 🙂
I’m someone you can rely on6 —when I make a commitment to you, I’ll be 100% present.
I try to live this life well. I’m pretty goofy around my friends and people I trust. That said, I find myself drawn to more spontaneous people, probably because I tend to be more reserved. Well:

professional life.

This could be us, "Before Sunset (2004)".

professional life.

This could be us, "Before Sunset (2004)".

I was an early inference optimization engineer7 at BentoML before Modular acquired us. In early May 2026, Qualcomm acquired Modular. I’m now at NVIDIA working on vLLM and supporting pretraining Nemotron.
I take my work seriously. I interned at the business analytics division of a bank back in 2018, doing behavioral analysis on customer usage patterns.
This was my first real exposure to supervised learning⁠ and I was immediately hooked.
I pretty much didn’t know a thing back then, but that didn’t bother me much: I found the problem fascinating and knew I would try to solve it, because I wanted to. I definitely still have a ton to learn, but over time you tend to pick up skills along the way.
Early on, I noticed that most of ML‘s technical debt comes down to scaling, which inherently is an engineering problem.
This led me to join BentoML, as a software engineer. The mission statement and positioning have shifted quite a bit since then, but the core remains the same: optimizing statistical models to be as fast and accessible as possible.
My approach to problems has stayed consistent since I learned arithmetic: don’t quit, managed obsession8, and get your hands dirty9.
I might not be good at something initially, but i find being autistic enough to care about a specific domain (scaling intelligence) has got me to a spot that makes 5-year-old Aaron proud.
I have some research interests I’m currently chasing — read them if you’re curious. I know it’s a bit long, so feel free to skip to the next topic. Otherwise hopefully it captures what I’m fascinated with as of Oct, 2025.

personal life.
That said, I care deeply about the well-being of the people around me. My headspace⁠ has been occupied with a lot lately, but I always try to stay present and make time for the people in my life. This might be connected to something else, though—I moved abroad at 17 to study at a private all-boys boarding school in Vancouver, and I think that left me a bit more anxious than I’d like to admit10.
My mom says I was always shy growing up. These days I’m much more social, though I suppose the right word is ambivert: I’m comfortable in social settings, but I also treasure my alone time.

Friends mean the world to me. I’d go so far as to say my whole model of relationships came out of my friendships:
One cannot be a friend to many people in the sense of having friendship of the perfect type with them, just as one cannot be in love with many people at once (for love is a sort of excess of feeling, and it is the nature of such only to be felt towards one person); and it is not easy for many people at the same time to please the same person very greatly, or perhaps even to be good in his eyes.Aristotle, Nicomachean Ethics, VIII
I love my friends deeply—so much that I’d willingly take a bullet for any of them, at any moment. There are no ulterior motives here; everything I do comes from genuine intention. When I find something really cool and share it with someone, it’s because they’re the first person who comes to mind. Part of me wishes that one day I’ll be able to give each of them the time and energy they truly deserve.
A scene in "Lost in Translation (2003)". I do sometimes, think about the time I wronged my friends. But it happened for a reason, and we learnt to grow from our mistakes.
So, yes, I care. I care a lot about people, both in its abstract and physical form. I try my hardest to amplify those around me and give them space to grow and achieve what they want in life (also another thing my dear mom taught me 🙂)

cooking

I love food. Michelin-starred chefs spend decades on one cuisine—I find that obsession beautiful.
Cooking a dish start-to-finish is the closest thing I have to therapy.
It’s also how I show love to my friends.
Every week I make fresh tortellinirotation of fillings includes ricotta-based, mushroom, and meat-based. I try to make this at least once a month, depending on how busy life gets., VeloutéConsidered one of the “mother sauces” by legendary chef Auguste Escoffier. There are many sauces that use Velouté as bases icymi., and tagliatelle11—this is my form of therapy.
I’m conscious about what I eat and try to substitute for organic ingredients when possible.
I do follow a carnivore diet myself, but I’m happy to cook anything.
I learned how to cook through books (Alice Waters and Thomas Keller’s), friends, and my mom.

Music is a huge part of my life—I honestly wouldn’t be able to function without it.
I prefer classical orchestra, a mix of blues and jazz, 80s rock, and I have a deep appreciation for house and garage culture.

Historically speaking, my past relationships have been polyamorous. I found that my work schedule fits well with that style of romantic attachment, and I’m definitely not the jealous type. Though my previous partner and I ended on a sour note, I’m more than happy with the growth. I’ve been in one monogamous relationship since then, and found that monogamy suits me a lot better
I don’t want kids, yet, at least for the next five years.

We are young still, many things yet to be explored.
I want to be focused on my work and dedication to my craft.
I will pursue academia at some point, or at least work on my independent research.
That said, I’d make it work for the right person.


I care deeply about my friends, and I believe that as partners, we don’t have to do everything together.I definitely want to spend the majority of my time with you, but I’ll need “boys” time.
Most of my friends are female. I have very clear boundaries with friends, but I want all my female friendships—especially with N, C, Si—to remain strong.
There are a few special people in my life,I won’t disclose them here, to respect their privacy that I would also like to maintain strong connections with.Meaning, I would make plans to fly over and see them from time to time.
I currently live in Toronto, Canada. I’m open to long-distance (but prefer not to) if there’s a good chance we’d end up in the same city, assuming everything goes well! San Francisco, Berkeley, New York, and Boston are all possibilities.

I do plan to move back to the US in the future, in the next 5-7 years.

polyamorousI believe partners should provide certain functions to each other, and being in a relationship shouldn’t stop you from exploring something different and new.

what i’m offering in a relationship


I’m cautiously optimistic, sometimes a bit self-deprecating.


My attachment style has always been “securely attached”⁠, though I found that my previous partner was “anxious-preoccupied”⁠, which made it a bit easier to give them “words of affirmation”. I’m a caregiver at heart, so I definitely want to look after you.


I will cook for you. You don’t have to come into the kitchen, but you’re more than welcome to join.


My love languages⁠ are physical touch, and quality time. I think of a life partner as someone you’re mutually supportive of and committed to—someone you’re building something together with.


I will get you flowers and write you letters.

The pasta I make varies in shape, but it is always uovo pasta made with eggs and a mix of 00 flour and semolina. I usually use an 80:20 ratio. Both flours contain wheat and gluten, so this recipe is unsafe for a wheat allergy or celiac disease. A gluten-free meal needs different ingredients and protection from cross-contact.
I hit the farmers’ market every Sunday morning to get the freshest eggs possible. Ideally, the yolks should be super orange (I know this is hard to find in Ontario), but slightly yellow yolks work fine too.
For bucatini, I use the stand mixer’s pasta press. I roll sheet pasta and flat strands by hand. Here is a recipe that works for four servings:

\frac{3}{2} cups of flour | 227 grams (mixed at ratio mentioned above)
1 tablespoon extra-virgin olive oil
3 yolks + 1 whole eggs
water as needed to bring the dough together
